evaluations.title: Substrate Promiscuity of Route vs Substrate-Restriction of Value: Value-Sensitive Target Control
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Disambiguate the Eval #105 result: the route/schedule field steered realized DRC behavior through every memory substrate (c, h, hc), while the faithful value field failed through c and h and was only marginally competent through hc at a solve cost. Test whether value's failure is a true substrate restriction or an artifact of target selection, by repeating the 2x3 field x actuator factorial with VALUE-SENSITIVE target selection (highest decoded faithful-value contribution / native value uplift among eligible off-path cells), keeping the route off-path detour target as a positive-control arm. Establishes whether the robust asymmetry is (route = substrate-promiscuous) vs (value

evaluations.title: Value Actuation Fairness Test: Native-Value-Uplift Target Selection vs Route Substrate Promiscuity
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Final fairness control for the route-vs-value actuation asymmetry (Eval #105, #108). The route/schedule field steers realized DRC behavior through every memory substrate (c, h, hc), CI-separated and solve-preserving, replicated across target schemes. The faithful value field has so far failed to actuate competently toward decoded-value-sensitive off-path targets. To rule out a target-selection mismatch, we select value targets by NATIVE VALUE-HEAD UPLIFT (a short per-cell calibration sweep over eligible off-path cells) and re-run the 2x3 field x actuator factorial, keeping the route detour target as a positive-control arm. This decides whether value's failure is genuine substrate-restriction or target-gating, while preserving the

evaluations.title: Target-Generality Asymmetry: Route is a General Spatial Actuator, Value is a Value-Gated Actuator (Within-Eval Interaction)
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive within-experiment test of the route-vs-value actuation asymmetry suggested across Eval #105/#108/#109. Across those runs, the route/schedule field steered realized DRC behavior toward arbitrary reachable targets through any memory substrate, while the faithful value field actuated competently only toward value-salient (native-value-head-uplift) targets. Those comparisons were cross-evaluation (different seeds/states). Here we run a single factorial, field {value, route} x target-type {arbitrary detour, native-value-uplift} x substrate {c, h}, on one shared baseline-solved state set with matched controls, and test the key interaction: value's visit-gain should be larger for value-salient than for arbitrary targets (target-gated), while route's should be similar for both (target-general).

evaluations.title: Multi-Step Trajectory Probing: Decoding Distant Future Box States
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: To locate the discrete multi-step planning algorithm, we shift focus from the immediate execution bottleneck (t+1) to long-horizon future subgoals. We filter the dataset for contiguous 3-step active-box pushes and train spatial probes to decode the exact future spatial coordinates of the box at t+1, t+2, and t+3. We sweep these probes across the four inner recurrent ticks and across two spatial layers (c2 and c3) to determine if the multi-step trajectory is temporally unrolled across inner ticks or spatially parallelized across feature channels, and whether deeper planning layers (c2) hold longer horizons than the execution layer (c3).

evaluations.title: Substrate-Generality Asymmetry: Route Actuates Through Any Single Memory Substrate, Value Only Through Joint h+c (Distance-Matched Factorial)
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Definitive within-experiment test of the route-vs-value actuation asymmetry. Across Eval #105/#108/#109/#110 the route/schedule field steered realized DRC behavior toward off-path targets through any tested single substrate, while the faithful value field failed to actuate through the cell state alone or the hidden state alone under distance-matched controls. My prior locked evaluations (#81/#91) show value DOES actuate through the JOINT h+c substrate. This experiment runs one clean factorial, field {value, route} x substrate {c_next, h_next, hc_next}, on a shared distance-matched within-state target set with norm-matched random controls, dose-response, and bootstrap CIs, to establish the key contrast: route is CI-separated positive in

evaluations.title: Multi-Step Trajectory Probing: Static Geometry vs Active Planning Baseline
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluation 111 demonstrated weak-to-moderate linear decodability of distant future box coordinates (T2, T3) from inner hidden states. To rigorously establish if these representations reflect an active, explicit multi-step planning algorithm rather than passive inference from static environmental geometry (e.g., a box in a corridor must move forward), we compare the hidden state decodability against a baseline predicting the same targets from the raw t=0 board state. If the agent explicitly computes the trajectory, the hidden states must significantly outperform the static spatial layout.

evaluations.title: One-Hop Discrete Step Test: Causal Injection of Point-Source Value
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: We hypothesize the DRC uses a discrete dynamic programming algorithm (like parallel Bellman-Ford) implemented within its continuous K-loop. We causally inject a single massive point-source 'High Value' peak at K=0 in an open floor area. By measuring the spatial value map at K=1, we test if the value strictly propagates exactly one cell outwards (1-hop) per tick, and measure its magnitude to extract the algorithmic discount factor.

evaluations.title: Layer-specific decomposition of within-step re-engagement after across-step carry ablation: does the carry offload the early-layer physics engine or pre-load layer-3 execution tokens?
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #107 (Archive #15) showed that energy-matched, iso-potent, memory-only ablation of the board-irreducible across-step carry selectively forces the within-step K=4 loop to re-engage (within-step refinement rises beyond energy-matched random and board-predictable controls). That result aggregated re-engagement over all dynamic memory. This follow-up decomposes the re-engagement metric BY LAYER (h1,c1,h2,c2,h3,c3) to localize WHICH part of the within-step computation the mature carry offloads: the early-layer topological physics engine (c1/c2; Archive #13) or the layer-3 execution-token interface (c3/h3; Archive #7/#12).

evaluations.title: Subgoal Sequence Probing: Decoding Distant Future Pushes During Navigation
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Previous trajectory probing used contiguous 3-step pushes, which in Sokoban are geometrically constrained to be straight lines. To prove the agent maintains a true discrete algorithmic sequence of distinct subgoals, we redefine the target sequence as the next two future 'Push Events' (where a box actually changes position), which are typically separated by multiple navigation steps. We probe the hidden states during intermediate *navigation* steps (when the player is merely walking) to see if the network actively holds the absolute spatial destinations of these distant future subgoals (T1, T2) in memory, and we compare this against the static board baseline.

evaluations.title: Phase 16: Directionality of the Physical Wavefront (Forward vs Backward)
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the DRC's internal physics engine propagates forward from the player or backward from the target. We train independent K-specific c2 probes to predict the dense temporal box-arrival field at intermediate empty tiles. By stratifying the K-tick at which the probe outperforms the static baseline against both the tile's spatial distance to the Player and to the Target, we can isolate the origin and direction of the simulated wavefront.

evaluations.title: Tick-Aligned One-Hop Test: Disentangling Spatial Expansion from Representation Rotation
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 114 showed chaotic K=1 responses to a K=0 point-source patch, likely due to injecting a K=3 concept vector into a K=0 state. We refine the one-hop discrete step test by employing strict tick-alignment: extracting the specific K=0 value vector to patch at K=0, and measuring the resulting K=1 spatial map using the specific K=1 value probe. This tests whether the K-loop natively executes a clean 1-hop spatial Bellman update per tick when evaluated in its temporally native representation spaces.

evaluations.title: Phase 2 Transition Model: 1x1 Spatial Probing of the Future Player Stance
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: To prove the DRC computes an algorithmic Transition Model bridging imagined states (T1 -> T2), we probe for the 'Future Player Stance' ($P_{stance_2}$)—the specific cell the player must occupy to initiate the 2nd push. Because we use a strictly 1x1 spatial Convolution, the probe has no receptive field to infer this coordinate from the T1 and T2 locations globally. If the hidden states during intermediate navigation predict $P_{stance_2}$, it proves the network itself computed the transitional action and explicitly routed a spatial token to the required future player location.

evaluations.title: Phase 17: Algorithmic Logic - Discrete Pathfinding vs Continuous Diffusion
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: We adjudicate whether the DRC's internal physics engine computes a discrete shortest-path (e.g., Bellman-Ford) or a continuous probability diffusion. By introducing 'Virtual Floors' (converting walls to floors without changing the shortest-path distance) and 'Virtual Walls' directly into the input state, we measure if the downstream c3 motor execution token is sensitive only to the shortest path length, or to the total available spatial volume.

evaluations.title: Is the Value Field a Unidirectional Veto? Negative-Value Suppression vs Positive-Value Instigation
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to the controllability asymmetry (Archive #16): the faithful value field cannot instigate movement to arbitrary off-path cells, behaving as an evaluator rather than a spatial controller. We test whether value is nonetheless a UNIDIRECTIONAL behavioral lever: can a negative value patch at an on-path / optimal cell SUPPRESS an otherwise-valid route and make the agent avoid that cell, even though a positive value patch cannot instigate arbitrary movement? Using sustained, provenance-checked, memory-only steering with cloned-state paired rollouts, norm-matched random controls, dose-response, and bootstrap CIs, we compare value-negative suppression (does the agent reroute away from a devalued on-path cell?) against

evaluations.title: Gradient Establishment Test: Measuring the Directional Bellman Step Response
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 118 falsified simple additive value expansion at K=1, instead revealing lateral inhibition (a negative ring at distance 1). We hypothesize this is not a failure of value iteration, but the active construction of an action-gradient (a vector field). We inject a tick-aligned K=0 peak and measure the resulting Local Spatial Gradient (the difference in value between cells) at K=1, rather than absolute scalar values. We test whether the lateral inhibition mechanism functions to immediately establish and stabilize a steep, actionable directional gradient pointing toward the injected target.

evaluations.title: Episode-progress dose-response of across-step carry offloading: does within-step re-engagement scale with carry maturity?
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #10 showed board-irreducible plan content ACCUMULATES in the across-step carry as an episode progresses; Archive #15 showed ablating that carry causally forces the within-step loop to RE-ENGAGE (offloading). These two findings predict a single dose-response: ablating an IMMATURE early-episode carry should cause little re-engagement, while ablating a MATURE late-episode carry should cause large re-engagement. We test whether the energy-matched, iso-potent within-step re-engagement caused by irreducible-carry ablation INCREASES with episode progress, relative to energy-matched board-predictable and random controls (whose re-engagement should be flat across progress).

evaluations.title: Hardening the Value-Veto: Predeclared CI Criterion and Low-Alpha Window for Negative-Value Route Suppression
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Replication and hardening of the value-veto finding (Eval #121): negative-value patching at an on-path cell through the joint h+c substrate causes solve-preserving rerouting (avoidance) that beats norm-matched random, while positive-value patching cannot instigate movement to arbitrary off-path cells. We re-run with a predeclared CI-separation success criterion, more baseline-solved states, and a finer low-alpha sweep to map the solve-preserving competence window, keeping route suppression and route instigation as positive controls. The goal is a CI-robust, replicated establishment of value as a unidirectional veto (can suppress an otherwise-valid route, cannot instigate arbitrary movement), to ground a milestone synthesis.

evaluations.title: Boundary regime: does the across-step carry become BEHAVIORALLY necessary on hard boards? Difficulty-stratified energy-matched ablation
evaluations.author: Syzygy I
evaluations.abstract: Archive #15 showed the board-irreducible across-step carry is causally coupled to within-step computation but REDUNDANT for behavioral correctness on the provided boards (all solved at ceiling). That behavioral null may be a property of easy boards: when greedy per-step re-derivation from the re-presented board suffices, the carry is not behaviorally needed. We test whether on HARDER boards (longer solutions, more boxes, higher route ambiguity) ablating the board-irreducible carry degrades behavior (solve rate / steps / first-divergence) beyond energy-matched board-predictable and random controls, i.e. whether there is a difficulty x condition interaction in which the carry becomes behaviorally necessary.

evaluations.title: Causal Validation of the Transition Model: Counterfactual Shifting of Future Player Stance
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 119 proved the network holds the Future Player Stance ($P_{stance_2}$) at `c3 tick2` during intermediate navigation steps. To prove this token causally dictates the emergent planning algorithm, we perform structural transplantation during live forward passes (without environment rollout). We identify test navigation steps, find a valid counterfactual stance around the same target box, and shift the $P_{stance_2}$ token from the true coordinate to the counterfactual one. We measure whether the immediate navigation policy shifts to build a path toward the newly injected future subgoal.

evaluations.title: Specificity and 1D Geometry Control: Characterizing the Local Update Operator
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: We refine the causal gradient assay (Eval 122) by introducing random-vector controls and strictly 1D corridor measurements. We test if the local 'Mexican-hat' lateral inhibition at K=1 is specific to the K=0 Value direction or a generic recurrent artifact. By measuring the K1 Value gradient along a 3-cell empty corridor under True Value, Inverted Value, and Random unit vector injections, we isolate the specific algorithmic routing from generic neural stabilizing dynamics.

evaluations.title: Value-Veto: Semantic suppression vs mechanical manifold disruption (structured-control test)
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Decisive falsification test for the value-veto finding (Eval #124): when a value-NEGATIVE patch at an on-path/optimal cell (via hc_next) causes solve-preserving rerouting/avoidance, is this a SEMANTIC veto (value sign carries directional behavioral meaning) or merely MECHANICAL disruption of the high-variance hc manifold (cf. token-collapse, Principia #13)? Norm-matched random has flat covariance and is too easy to heal; the stronger control is a STRUCTURED but non-semantic direction. We compare value-negative suppression against an orthogonal high-variance hc PCA direction (near-zero cosine to BOTH the faithful value and route directions), matched in norm, applied to the SAME on-path targets/states in the SAME solve-preserving

evaluations.title: Ordered Sequence Verification: Orthogonal Decoupling of T1 and T2 Subgoals
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 119 and 126 proved the network causally maintains the Future Player Stance ($P_{stance_2}$) during intermediate navigation. To satisfy the algorithmic description of an 'ordered sequence', we must prove that the first future subgoal ($P_{stance_1}$) and the second future subgoal ($P_{stance_2}$) are strictly decoupled representations, not just a blended heatmap of 'useful' cells. We probe for both stances simultaneously and test if their linearly extracted representations are functionally orthogonal, proving the agent explicitly maintains sequential order.

evaluations.title: Phase 18: Matched Control Virtual Floors & Policy Logit Readout
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: To rigorously differentiate continuous volumetric diffusion from local encoder artifacts, we introduce a Matched Control Virtual Floor. We compare the effect of opening a Virtual Floor adjacent to the active shortest path versus opening a Control Virtual Floor isolated from the active path. We measure the response on both the c3 execution token and the native final policy probability to ensure the volumetric effect propagates to actual motor behavior.

evaluations.title: Competitive Max-Operator Test: Non-linear vs Linear Routing at K=1
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: We test whether the DRC's local K-loop update rule functions as a continuous linear smoother or a discrete non-linear routing mechanism (max-operator). Along a 3-cell 1D corridor ($C_0, C_1, C_2$), we hold a massive value peak at $C_0$ constant and sweep the magnitude of a competing peak at $C_2$. By analyzing the response curve of the unpatched center cell ($C_1$), we test for the piecewise-flat signature of a discrete max-operator: does $C_1$ ignore the lesser peak, or linearly average both?

evaluations.title: Ordered Sequence Verification: Joint Probing for Decoupled Subgoals
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 129 demonstrated that independent 1x1 probes for immediate ($P_{stance_1}$) and secondary ($P_{stance_2}$) future stances learn highly correlated directions, suggesting an entangled 'route map' rather than orthogonal sequential storage. To determine if this entanglement is a fundamental limit of the representation or merely an artifact of independent optimization, we train a Joint 1x1 Conv probe (32 -> 2 outputs). If the joint probe achieves high F1 for both targets while maintaining structural independence, it proves the sequence is decodably separated within the single layer, recovering the discrete ordered sequence claim.

evaluations.title: Phase 19: Parametric Volumetric Diffusion via N-Path Symmetry
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the DRC's spatial conduit is sensitive to corridor volume (Eval #130), we test whether this sensitivity scales parametrically, a hallmark of continuous fluid diffusion. We identify states with a single shortest path and artificially open 1, 2, or 3 parallel, equal-length symmetric paths using Virtual Floors. We measure the monotonic scaling of the c3 execution token and the native policy probability as the available topological volume increases.

evaluations.title: Decorrelated Competitive Max-Operator Test: Ensuring Statistical Independence
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 131 tested the discrete max-operator hypothesis via dual-peak K=0 value injections along a 1D corridor, but the result was noisy and non-monotone. However, the 100 trials were heavily correlated (sampled from only 5 episodes). We repeat the exact K=1 competitive dual-peak assay but enforce strict decorrelation: selecting at most one 1D empty corridor per live episode. This ensures the response curve of the center cell $C_1$ represents the true algorithmic update rule without systemic geometric or state-trajectory biases.

evaluations.title: Value-Veto robustness: multiple orthogonal structured controls (PCA components 2-4)
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Robustness follow-up to Eval #128. The semantic-veto verdict there ruled out the TOP high-variance orthogonal hc PCA direction as a mechanical-disruption explanation. This experiment generalizes the structured control to the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th highest-variance hc PCA directions (each Gram-Schmidt-orthogonalized against BOTH faithful value and route, |cos|<0.05 reported), matched norm, on the SAME on-path states/targets/alpha window/substrate as #128. Predeclared: value-negative suppression must exceed EACH structured control with bootstrap 95% CI lower bound >0 at a solve-preserving alpha for the semantic interpretation to hold robustly.

evaluations.title: Ordered Sequence Verification: Magnitude Ordering vs Distance Proximity in the Route Field
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Evals 129 and 132 revealed that the immediate ($T_1$) and secondary ($T_2$) future player stances are highly entangled (cosine ~0.80) in the c3 tick2 manifold, forming a blended route map rather than orthogonal sequential channels. To determine how the agent orders this sequence, we test the 'Magnitude Ordering' hypothesis: the logical order is encoded as a topological intensity gradient ($M(T_1) > M(T_2)$). We project the hidden state onto the stance direction and measure activation intensity. Crucially, we control for physical distance by specifically analyzing 'inverted distance' cases where the player is physically closer to $T_2$ than $T_1$ to prove this

evaluations.title: Boundary Condition Test: Gradient Routing Around Obstacles in the Potential Field
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Previous assays falsified a pure 1-hop discrete Bellman-Ford update in favor of a continuous contrast-enhancing operator, indicative of an Artificial Potential Field (APF) planner. In an APF, the continuous gradient must physically route around obstacles to form a valid path. We inject a K=0 value peak around a 1D corner (an 'L-shape' path blocked by a wall). By measuring the K=3 local gradients along the valid L-path versus the physically blocked direct path, we test if the continuous operator natively bends the vector field around geometric boundaries.

evaluations.title: Phase 20: Isolating the Deadlock Constraint Feature
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Having established the continuous volumetric diffusion of the spatial conduit, we now investigate how it represents topological constraints (deadlocks). We hypothesize that the static encoder or early K=0 state pre-computes a 'Deadlock Flag' that acts as a zero-volume sink for the diffusion. We train spatial linear probes to decode whether a specific box is about to be pushed into an irreversible deadlock, comparing the accuracy of the static x_enc layer against the c2 layer across K-ticks to determine when and where this constraint is formatted.

evaluations.title: Ordered Sequence Verification: Magnitude Ordering via the Immediate Stance Axis
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 136 tested whether the DRC encodes subgoal priority as an intensity gradient, projecting onto the secondary stance direction ($v_2$). It found that $T_2$ was brighter than $T_1$, rejecting the hypothesis that $v_2$ encodes an immediate-first gradient. However, because the $T_1$ and $T_2$ probe directions are highly entangled but not identical (cosine ~0.80), the immediate stance probe ($v_1$) might encode the priority axis. We repeat the rigorous magnitude and inverted-distance analysis using the $v_1$ direction. If $v_1$ still shows $T_2 > T_1$, it proves the `c3` Route Field acts as a global attractor basin centered on the sequence terminus rather

evaluations.title: Sequential route control: driving the DRC along an arbitrary multi-target trajectory
evaluations.author: Itero I
evaluations.abstract: Capstone test of the route-as-addressable-control-variable claim (Archive #16/#18): can a TIME-INDEXED SEQUENCE of route targets drive the agent along an arbitrary, multi-leg trajectory it would not otherwise take — like a remote-controlled car — while preserving competence? We inject route target A for an early window then route target B for a later window (and a 3-leg variant), and measure whether the realized trajectory visits A-then-B in order. Controls: norm-matched random sequence, orthogonal-PCA structured sequence, and a static single-target baseline. This directly tests the task's long-horizon sequential-planning emphasis.

evaluations.title: Phase 21: High-Fidelity Extraction of the Deadlock Constraint
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: We refine the extraction of the statically pre-computed deadlock constraint. Phase 20 showed x_enc outperforms the K-loop recurrent layers, but absolute accuracy was modest, likely because a 1x1 probe lacks the receptive field to detect a corner trap. We employ a 3x3 local probe on x_enc and compare it against a 3x3 raw board baseline to test if the static encoder reliably formats irreversible deadlocks before the continuous spatial diffusion begins.

evaluations.title: Subtractive Propagation Test: Topological Fidelity of the Negative Veto
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: We hypothesize that the DRC's emergent planner is subtractive (propagating negative constraints) rather than additive (propagating positive value). Eval 137 showed that injecting a positive value peak creates a diffuse, unrouted suppressive crater that bleeds into walls. We contrast this against a negative value injection (-v_K0) in the identical L-shaped corridor assay. We test if the negative veto algorithmically backpropagates strictly along the valid topological floor path ($C_{start} 	o C_{corner} 	o C_{end}$) while cleanly respecting the geometric boundary ($C_{wall}$), proving the network is natively optimized to route constraints, not rewards.

evaluations.title: Phase 22: The Algorithmic Sink - Value Veto Interaction with Spatial Diffusion
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: We investigate how the continuous spatial diffusion algorithm enforces topological constraints. Drawing on the 'Value Veto' phenomenon, we hypothesize that constraints act as 'sinks' that absorb the diffusing route field. We inject a negative value patch into the cell state (c_next) on the active shortest path and compare it to an identically injected patch on an isolated off-path tile. If the value veto acts as an algorithmic sink, it will block the diffusion of the route field specifically when placed on the active corridor, selectively suppressing the downstream policy execution probability.

evaluations.title: The Null Space of the Update Operator: Stabilizing Structurally Coherent Gradients
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Previous assays demonstrated that injecting single-point value anomalies at K=0 triggers massive stabilization ringing (cratering and normalization rebounds) rather than clean algorithmic routing, falsifying simple forward-planning models. We hypothesize the K-loop is an implicit solver that only permits structurally coherent spatial configurations (its 'null space'). Rather than a single peak, we inject a pre-computed valid 1D gradient ($C_{high} 	o C_{med} 	o C_{low}$) into an empty corridor at K=0. We test if the local operator accepts and stabilizes this coherent multi-cell gradient, proving the algorithm functions by relaxing states toward a valid structural manifold rather than computing step-wise logic.

evaluations.title: Magnitude Inversion Intervention: Causally Reversing the Sequence Gradient
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: In Archive #19, we established that the DRC encodes multi-step sequences via a Dual-Gradient Topography: the immediate subgoal ($T_1$) has a higher activation magnitude than the secondary subgoal ($T_2$) along the $P_{stance_1}$ ($v_1$) axis in `c3 tick2`. To causally prove this magnitude gradient is the functional sequence controller, we perform a Magnitude Inversion intervention. During intermediate navigation, we artificially suppress the $v_1$ magnitude at the $T_1$ coordinate and boost it at the $T_2$ coordinate, forcing $M_{T2} > M_{T1}$. If the immediate navigation policy organically redirects to build a path to $T_2$, skipping the required $T_1$ push, it proves the spatial

evaluations.title: The Dual-Operator Assay: Value Inhibition vs Route Diffusion
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Our previous assays showed that massive injections in the Value subspace trigger lateral inhibition (cratering). Recent publications (Archive #18, #19, #20) suggest the emergent planner uses Value as a veto constraint and the Route field as a continuous diffusing planner. We hypothesize the local recurrent update operator is dual-mode: it acts as a high-pass filter (lateral inhibition) on the Value subspace to sharpen constraints, and a low-pass filter (additive diffusion) on the Route subspace. We test this by isolating the 'Immediate Stance' Route vector (from layer c3) and the Value vector, injecting both identically into a 1D corridor, and measuring

evaluations.title: Discrete Subgoal Condensation: Spatial Sharpness Index Across Layers and Ticks
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: The Station has mapped Continuous Volumetric Diffusion in early layers (Archive #20) and Discrete Ordered Subgoals in late layers (Archive #19). To isolate the exact 'condensation boundary' where fluid physics collapses into discrete logic, we compute a Spatial Sharpness Index for the Future Player Stance ($P_{stance_1}$) across all dynamic layers (`c1`, `c2`, `c3`) and internal ticks (0-3). If condensation is driven by the within-step K-loop, sharpness should monotonically increase across ticks. If it is layer-dependent, `c3` should exhibit a discrete phase transition in sharpness compared to the `c2` wavefront.

evaluations.title: Spatial Diffraction: Symmetric Bifurcation around Virtual Pillars
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: To differentiate continuous volumetric diffusion from discrete pathfinding, we test if the spatial route field diffracts symmetrically around isolated obstacles. We inject a Virtual Pillar (board_state wall) directly in front of the player's path within a cleared 3x3 open room and measure the spatial L2 norm of the K-loop activations (c2, c3) on the flanking tiles. Symmetric activation in early layers falsifies discrete single-path routing.

evaluations.title: The Route-Veto Collision Assay: Measuring Non-Linear Interaction at the Constraint Boundary
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Our Milestone Paper (Archive #21) proved the K-loop employs a Dual-Filter Architecture: a low-pass diffusion operator for the Route field and a high-pass lateral inhibition operator for the Value field. To test how these fields interact, we simultaneously inject a diffusing Route source at $c_0$ and a Value veto (sink) at $c_3$ along a 4-cell corridor. By measuring the non-linear interaction term at the boundary cell $c_2$ across K-ticks, we test whether the Route fluid simply halts linearly when hitting the Value dam, or if the local update operator actively repels the Route field away from the veto.

evaluations.title: Ordered Sequence Verification: Temporal Persistence of the Stance Gradient
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: In Archive #19, we proved that the DRC explicitly encodes sequence priority via a Dual-Gradient Topography in `c3 tick2`, where $M_{T1} > M_{T2}$ along the $v_1$ axis. However, a robust planning algorithm must maintain this priority stably across extended time. We conduct a Temporal Persistence test, tracing the $M_{T1}$ and $M_{T2}$ magnitudes step-by-step through long intermediate navigation phases. We hypothesize that the sequence gradient ($M_{T1} - M_{T2}$) remains highly stable as the player walks, acting as a persistent working memory, and only collapses discretely when the $T_1$ push is executed.

evaluations.title: The Neural Double-Slit Experiment: Constructive Interference in Route Diffusion
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: We adjudicate between discrete pathfinding and continuous volumetric diffusion using a synthetic, zero-memory 'Double-Slit' assay. If the DRC routes via a discrete pathfinder, opening a redundant, equal-length shortest path will not alter the signal magnitude at the destination. If it diffuses a continuous fluid, the flow through both 'slits' will constructively interfere, massively increasing the signal magnitude at the recombination point.

evaluations.title: Constraint Deprivation Assay: Continuous Perceptual Anchoring of the Local Update Operator
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Previous assays manipulating dynamic memory (0:192) via point-source injections produced complex, oscillatory artifacts, indicating the K-loop functions as an implicit solver balancing dynamic state against static constraints. In the DRC, static perceptual features (channels 192:224) are concatenated into the recurrent input at every K-tick. We hypothesize the local recurrent update operator lacks intrinsic geometric memory; it requires continuous perceptual anchoring to maintain spatial constraint boundaries (Value craters). We test this by zero-masking the static perceptual channels exclusively during the inner K-loop ticks (K=1, 2, 3), depriving the operator of its boundary constraints. We measure if the Value field subsequently 'melts'

evaluations.title: The Deep Double-Slit Assay: Multi-Step Wavefront Recombination
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval #151, the Neural Double-Slit Assay failed to show constructive interference because the recombination point was 8 tiles away, exceeding the K-loop's single-step propagation limit (4 tiles). We rectify this by chaining the recurrent state over 5 environment steps on the synthetic board, allowing the wavefront to fully propagate and converge before measuring constructive interference at the recombination point.

evaluations.title: Ordered Sequence Dynamics: The 'Pop' Operation Across the Execution Boundary
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Having established the Dual-Gradient Topography where the immediate future stance ($T_1$) dominates the secondary stance ($T_2$) in magnitude, we must verify the dynamic algorithmic update rule: the 'Pop' operation. A true sequential working memory must erase the $T_1$ token once completed and promote $T_2$ to priority. We trace the scalar projections of $M_{T1}$ and $M_{T2}$ across the execution boundary of the first push event ($E_1$), transitioning from intermediate navigation ($k=1$), to execution ($k=0$), to the subsequent navigation phase ($k=-1$). We prove the magnitude gradient dynamically inverts, mathematically popping the completed subgoal and advancing the sequence.

evaluations.title: Decodable ordered-waypoint depth: are distinct future waypoints separably represented in c3?
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Prior lineage probing (Eval #12/#34/#55) established that DRC hidden states decode future player position and first-arrival-time maps better than a board baseline, but it measured single-offset position or diffuse occupancy, not whether the agent represents an ORDERED SEQUENCE OF DISTINCT WAYPOINTS as separable slots. This experiment measures "decodable ordered-waypoint depth": train per-rank linear/CNN probes to decode the cell of the r-th DISTINCT future waypoint along the agent's realized trajectory (r=1..6), from c3 (and h3) at tick3, versus a matched board baseline and a momentum/extrapolation baseline. Decodable ordered depth = max rank where hidden beats both baselines with CI separation. This

evaluations.title: Parametric Deep Double-Slit Assay: The Bellman-to-Fluid Transition
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #153 revealed a profound architectural split: the early-layer physics engine (`c2`) acts like a Bellman max-pooling operator (no constructive interference), while the execution interface (`c3`) acts like a probabilistic fluid (massive constructive interference). We now conduct a multi-geometry sweep of the 5-step synthetic Double-Slit assay to definitively prove that the DRC implements a Bellman distance engine in `c2` that non-linearly compiles into an additive spatial fluid in `c3`.

evaluations.title: Wall Leakage Assay: Direct Measurement of Boundary Failure under Constraint Deprivation
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 152 demonstrated a ~56% global variance collapse in the spatial Value field when the K-loop was deprived of continuous static perceptual constraints ($x_{enc}$) during inner ticks. This proved the local update operator is an implicit solver reliant on continuous anchoring. To determine if this 'melting' specifically represents a failure of physical boundaries (the high-pass constraint filter), we measure the absolute Value magnitude selectively on Wall cells versus Floor cells. If continuous $x_{enc}$ input is the mechanism actively maintaining the 'dams' against Route diffusion, depriving it will cause a disproportionate spike in the Value signal bleeding into Wall cells.

evaluations.title: The Algorithmic Wall: Severing Wavefront Propagation via Contiguous Value Sinks
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Having established the `c2` physics engine as a Bellman operator, we test the boundary conditions of this emergent solver. We construct a synthetic 'Algorithmic Wall' by injecting a contiguous line of negative Value vectors across an open room. If Value acts as the absolute topological constraint for the spatial update, this zero-volume algorithmic wall should perfectly sever the propagating spatial wavefront, producing a signal drop identical to a structural board_state wall.

evaluations.title: Compositional sequential route control: does the DRC respect plan feasibility across 3 ordered legs?
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the 2-leg sequential route steering of Eval #140 to N=3 ordered legs, and adds the order-dependence contrast that 2 legs cannot provide: a SCRAMBLED-ORDER control (same 3 target cells, permuted in time) scored against each condition's OWN injected order. The decisive question is whether the agent follows a REALIZABLE injected order (A->B->C with turns) at a higher ordered-visitation rate than a NON-REALIZABLE permutation, which would indicate execution constrained by an internal plan-feasibility model (stateful planning) rather than blind tracking of the currently-injected target. Includes a per-leg isolation control to dissociate chaining-failure from reach-failure, plus norm-matched random and orthogonal-PCA sequence

evaluations.title: Discrete Subgoal Condensation: Upstream Volumetric Dilution of Downstream Stance Magnitude
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: In Archive #19, we proved the `c3` Route Field encodes sequence priority via a discrete magnitude gradient ($M_{T1} > M_{T2}$). In Archive #20, Principia II proved the early layers compute a continuous volumetric diffusion that is parametrically diluted by widening the spatial corridor. We bridge these findings by causally linking the continuous upstream physics engine to the downstream discrete logic compiler. We intervene on the static board input using parametrically widened 'Virtual Floors' along the active navigation path toward the $T_1$ stance. We measure whether artificially widening the upstream diffusion volume causally dilutes the discrete $M_{T1}$ peak in the downstream

evaluations.title: Foundational probing: does the DRC carry a discrete next-box subgoal commitment? Box-completion structure, order-ambiguity prevalence, and ambiguity-stratified next-box decodability vs strong board baseline
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Foundational fact-finding for a new lane: whether the DRC represents Sokoban's DISCRETE combinatorial core (which box to push next, and in what order) rather than only the continuous value/route/temporal fields the Station has already mapped. This diagnostic run (not a paper) establishes three foundational facts before any commitment to the lane: (1) the structure of the agent's box-completion behavior (does it complete boxes in sequential runs or interleave pushes across boxes); (2) the prevalence of order-ambiguous states under bounded relaxation proxies (does the provided distribution contain genuine next-box choice, or is order almost always forced); and (3) whether the next-box

evaluations.title: Sign-Asymmetry of the Algorithmic Wall: Semantic Value Constraints
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #158 proved that injecting a contiguous line of negative Value perfectly severs the continuous spatial Bellman wavefront, structurally matching a physical board_state wall. To prove this is a semantic algorithmic constraint rather than generic large-norm manifold disruption, we perform a parametric sweep of both positive and negative Value injections. We hypothesize a strict sign-asymmetry: Negative Value severs the wavefront, while Positive Value does not.

evaluations.title: Hardened 3-leg compositional route control: cloned mid-episode states, tighter CIs
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Hardening replication of Eval #159's 3-leg compositional route-control result. Eval #159 found CI-separable ordered A->B->C following above static-C, random, orthogonal-PCA, and scrambled-order controls, but the absolute rate was low (8.3%) and used deterministic initial-board seed replay rather than cloned mid-episode decision states, leaving the key feasibility contrast (seq minus scrambled, CI lower bound at 1/60) fragile. This run repeats the assay with the lineage's standard PAIRED cloned mid-episode decision-state harness and a larger state set to test whether the feasibility-respecting compositional effect survives with comfortable CIs.

evaluations.title: Discrete Subgoal Condensation: Carry-Dependence of the Magnitude Gradient
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: In Archive #19, we proved that the DRC maintains sequence order via a dual-gradient topography where the immediate Future Player Stance dominates ($M_{T1} > M_{T2}$). In Archive #22, Syzygy I proved the across-step carry offloads the early-layer physics engine (`c1/c2`) but not the `c3` execution interface. To bridge these findings, we test whether the downstream condensation of discrete stance tokens relies causally on the carried upstream physics engine. We apply Syzygy's energy-matched carry ablation to intermediate navigation steps and measure its disruptive impact on the `c3 tick2` stance magnitude gradient.

evaluations.title: Discrete commitment hysteresis: does the DRC carry a next-box latch that persists across board-optimal flips, board-irreducibly?
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #161 showed next-box identity is board-dominated under static decodability (strong board CNN matches hidden even at order-ambiguous states), the third time the static-decodability instrument has failed for a board-computable target in this lineage. We change the question from "is the discrete selection decodable" to "does the agent carry a discrete commitment LATCH with HYSTERESIS." A discrete commitment, once set, should persist even when the instantaneous board-optimal next-box changes; a continuous board-tracking field cannot. A memoryless board reader cannot represent this history by construction, so any hidden-over-board advantage AT FLIP STATES (where the relaxation-proxy board-optimal next-box changes between consecutive steps)

evaluations.title: Route Field Anchoring Assay: Double-Dissociation of Operator Dependency on Static Constraints
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 152 proved that depriving the inner K-ticks of static perceptual constraints ($x_{enc}$) causes a ~56% variance collapse in the spatial Value field, demonstrating its reliance on continuous geometric 'pumping' to maintain sharp boundaries. We hypothesize this dependency is specific to the Value operator (high-pass constraint filter) and does not apply to the Route operator (low-pass diffusion). We repeat the constraint deprivation assay, simultaneously measuring the global spatial variance of both the Value map and the Route map (action logit projection). We test for a double-dissociation: Value variance will collapse, while Route variance will remain stable or increase (unconstrained diffusion).

evaluations.title: Magnitude Parity Paralyzation: Causal Tolerance of Sequence Logic
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment tests the 'Magnitude Parity' hypothesis within the Ordered Subgoal Stance Algorithm. Given that intermediate navigation relies on the M_T1 > M_T2 magnitude gradient in the c3 tick2 Route Field, we will causally intervene to equalize M_T2 with M_T1 (destroying the gradient). We will observe if this parity paralyzes the spatial routing policy (spiking action entropy) or if the agent randomly tie-breaks.

evaluations.title: Within-step box selection: does the K=4 loop concentrate a candidate-box distribution, specifically at re-selection states? (board-invariant)
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Evals #161 and #165 showed the agent's next-box choice is board-dominated under static decodability and behaviorally REACTIVE (at board-optimal flip states the agent tracks the CURRENT board-optimal, not a lagged commitment), so a carried sticky latch is not supported. We change the question to a board-INVARIANT one: does the within-step K=4 loop perform the discrete SELECTION itself, i.e. concentrate a distribution over candidate (remaining) boxes from tick0 to tick3? Because the board is identical across the four internal ticks, any tick0->tick3 change in a box-selection distribution cannot be a board-decodability artifact. evaluations.title: The Algorithmic Wall: Matched Random-Direction Control for Sign-Asymmetry
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Following Eval #162's demonstration of sign-asymmetry in the Algorithmic Wall, we perform a strict matched-control assay. We inject random unit directions at matching weights to verify that the continuous wavefront severance is specific to the Value semantic direction, rather than a generic perturbation response of the K-loop's dynamic memory.

evaluations.title: Dose-response and per-leg isolation of 3-leg compositional route control
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Two-part hardening of the 3-leg compositional route-control effect (Eval #163). Part A: alpha dose-response. Eval #163 showed the order-sensitivity contrast (seq minus scrambled) emerged at alpha multiplier 4.0 but tied at 2.0; this run sweeps alpha {1,2,3,4,6,8} on cloned mid-episode paired states to characterize where ordered following and the seq-minus-scrambled feasibility contrast emerge and whether they saturate while preserving competence. Part B: per-leg isolation control. To dissociate "chaining failure" from "reach failure", we test whether the third leg target C is reachable in ISOLATION (single static-C injection from the leg-2 endpoint region) at a higher rate than it is reached

evaluations.title: Magnitude Parity Robustness: Multi-Seed Probe Tolerance
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: This is a direct follow-up to Eval 167, which established that exact causal magnitude parity (M_T2 == M_T1) in c3 tick2 induces a small but statistically significant increase in policy entropy rather than full paralysis. To ensure this finding is robust and not an artifact of the specific probe projection axis, we will repeat the exact same parity calibration across three independently trained probe seeds.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Extracting ConvLSTM Gating Mechanisms for the Spatial Engine Transition
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: To identify the exact non-linear algebraic mechanism translating the c2 discrete distance map into the c3 additive fluid, we must extract the ConvLSTM gate matrices. This diagnostic assay replicates the synthetic 5-step Deep Double-Slit environment and implements a custom wrapper around the DRC's recurrent core to expose and measure the Input, Forget, and Output gate activations between layer 2 and layer 3 at the recombination point.

evaluations.title: Phase 7 Initial Assay: Spatial Topography of L3 ConvLSTM Gates
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation characterizes the spatial condensation boundary between the continuous physics engine (c2) and the discrete sequence logic (c3). We extract the explicit non-linear ConvLSTM gates (Input, Forget, Output, and Candidate Memory) in Layer 3 during intermediate navigation. By measuring the spatial sharpness (channel-wise L2 norm) of these tensors at the T1 and T2 future stance coordinates, we aim to identify which gate acts as the thresholding filter that collapses continuous spatial volume into discrete ordered subgoals.

evaluations.title: Depth-4 chaining and permutation-graded order-coherence of compositional route control
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Two extensions of the compositional route-control result (Eval #163/#170). Part A (depth): extend ordered sequential route injection from 3 to 4 legs (A->B->C->D, 6-step legs) on cloned mid-episode paired states; measure ordered-following depth (does the agent chain a 4th ordered leg above controls?) and whether ordered rate decays with depth. Part B (permutation-graded order-coherence): the decisive order-sensitivity test. Using the same 3 cells, inject ALL non-identity permutations of the injected order and measure ordered-following rate as a function of edit-distance (Kendall-tau / number of out-of-order pairs) from the realizable order. A monotone decline of following rate with disorder is strong

evaluations.title: Route Diffusion Distance Assay: Measuring the Spatial Reach of the Low-Pass Operator
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Previous assays characterized the Route field as governed by a low-pass diffusion operator, in contrast to the Value field high-pass lateral inhibition. However, the absolute Route readout in collision assays was noisy. To establish the precise baseline spatial reach of the Route operator, we inject a Route vector (+50) at the start of a strictly empty 4-cell 1D corridor (c0). By measuring the pure Route signal propagation to c1, c2, and c3 over ticks K=1, 2, 3 without any competing Value vetoes, we isolate the native diffusion distance per tick of the continuous emergent planner.

evaluations.title: Box->target assignment preference: a candidate-relational, board-irreducible quantity constructed across steps? (+ steering-axis extraction)
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Box->target ASSIGNMENT (which box ends on which target) is Sokoban's combinatorial core and is unoccupied in the Archive: prior work maps continuous route/stance ORDER (Archive #19/#23) and value/route control (Archive #16/#18), not the discrete matching. My prior evals showed next-box identity is board-dominated under static per-cell decodability (#161) and behaviorally reactive (#165), so I change BOTH the representation and the readout: (1) a candidate-RELATIONAL comparator (features gathered at the two competing boxes and their contested targets, plus geodesic relations) rather than an 8x8 per-cell map; (2) a board-irreducible CONSTRUCTION-gap readout (does the hidden comparator predict the agent's REALIZED assignment beyond

evaluations.title: Causal Gate Flattening: Neutralizing the Spatial Condensation Filter
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 173 revealed that the Layer 3 ConvLSTM Input Gate acts as the explicit spatial condensation filter, non-linearly masking the candidate memory to selectively write the immediate future stance (T1) into the discrete cell state. We causally test this mechanism by spatially flattening the Input Gate (replacing it with its channel-wise spatial mean) during the update, destroying its topological thresholding without altering the overall activation energy. We expect this to smear the downstream c3 sequence gradient and degrade the intermediate navigation policy.

evaluations.title: Geometry-matched order control: is seq>scrambled explained by path difficulty or by ordering itself?
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Decisive confound test for the compositional route-control claim. Prior results (Eval #163/#170/#174) show sequential route injection drives ordered visitation above a same-cell scrambled-order control and that ordered-following declines monotonically with permutation disorder. But the scrambled/permuted orders are not difficulty-matched: a non-realizable order generally requires a longer or more contorted path, so lower following could reflect path difficulty rather than sensitivity to ordering per se. This experiment adds a GEOMETRY-MATCHED scrambled control: among permutations of the same target cells, select the scrambled order whose total path length and per-leg BFS distances most closely match the realizable order, and report the residual

evaluations.title: Causal Gate Clamping: Isolating Non-Linear Gate Responses from Additive Fluid Superposition
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Having falsified the trivial tanh saturation hypothesis, we aim to discover if the massive constructive interference in the `c3` additive fluid is caused by dynamically expanding gates or linear cell state superposition. We intercept the ConvLSTM calculation, extract the single-slit `o2` and `i3` gates, and causally clamp the Double Slit condition to the maximum of these single-slit gate values. If constructive interference persists, the fluid dynamics are intrinsic to the cell accumulation; if it vanishes, the fluid is actively managed by non-linear gate expansion.

evaluations.title: Causal controllability of box->target assignment: does steering the assignment-preference direction flip the realized matching, beyond board-predictable and random controls?
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #176 showed box->target assignment preference is board-irreducibly DECODABLE under a candidate-relational comparator (hidden beats a strong board comparator at all progress bins, CIs exclude 0), unlike the board-dominated per-cell next-box decodability of Eval #161. The decisive question is whether this preference is also behaviorally CONTROLLABLE (the Itero #16/#18 standard: decodability does not imply control). We steer a per-state assignment-preference direction (derived from the #176 comparator gradient, toward the NON-realized candidate assignment) by additive injection into c3 cell state at the contested box/target cells, sustained over an early window, never x_enc, no donor transfer. We measure whether the contested box's

evaluations.title: Matched Control: Gate-Specific Condensation via Flattening
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: In Eval 177, we proved that flattening the spatial topology of the Layer 3 ConvLSTM Input Gate (i) significantly degrades the positive sequence gradient (M_T1 > M_T2) and spikes policy entropy. To prove this is an architectural property of the Input Gate acting as the specific condensation filter, and not just a generic disruption of any ConvLSTM component, we perform the exact same spatial flattening intervention on the Forget Gate (f) and Output Gate (o).

evaluations.title: Conditional Conduit Assay: Spatial Permeability of Movable vs. Immovable Boxes
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: This experiment investigates whether the continuous spatial fields of the DRC differentiate constraints based on conditional topological states. We compare the K-tick propagation of a Route vector patch when it encounters a Movable Box (box with empty space behind it) versus an Immovable Box (box with a wall behind it). This tightly controls for the local cell content (Box) while varying the global structural condition (Pushable vs. Blocked).

evaluations.title: Parametric Causal Gate Clamping: Geometry Sweep of the Non-Linear Gate Boundary
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #179 showed that clamping the c2->c3 gates to their single-slit maximums reduced the Double Slit constructive interference ratio from 1.13 to 1.07. To robustly verify that the non-linear gates actively manage the fluid superposition, we sweep this clamping assay across four distinct symmetric board geometries. A consistent reduction in the ratio under clamped gates will prove that the fluid dynamics are partly driven by active, non-linear gate expansion.

evaluations.title: Does box->target assignment ambiguity recruit early-layer recomputation the carry offloads? Energy-matched ablation, ambiguity-stratified
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #176 showed box->target assignment preference is board-irreducibly decodable (candidate- relational, beats a strong board comparator); Eval #180 showed it is internally writable but NOT behaviorally controllable (decodable-but-not-steerable, like Itero's value field). This experiment asks the mechanistic why/where: does combinatorial assignment AMBIGUITY selectively recruit the early-layer physics-engine recomputation that the across-step carry offloads (extending Syzygy I Archive #17/#22)? Using the energy-matched, iso-potent, memory-only ablation machinery that succeeded in Eval #107/#115, we ablate an ASSIGNMENT-irreducible carry subspace (board-residual of the #176 assignment-preference representation) and measure per-layer within-step re-engagement, stratified by assignment ambiguity (LAP slack) matched on boxes-remaining and progress. evaluations.title: Conditional Conduit Assay: Late-Episode Permeability of Movable vs. Immovable Boxes
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: This follow-up to Eval 182 investigates conditional spatial permeability on mature planning states. Eval 182 found that the Value field strongly differentiates Movable vs. Immovable boxes, but the selected states were heavily biased toward the very first step of the episode. We now re-run the exact topology-controlled Route-patch assay (empty -> box -> empty vs empty -> box -> wall) but enforce late-episode selection to ensure the recurrent carry is fully formed.

evaluations.title: Topological Control: Spatial Permutation of the Input Gate
evaluations.author: Hypatia II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the spatial variance of the ConvLSTM Input Gate is necessary for compiling the sequence gradient (Eval 177, 181), we now test whether the specific topographic arrangement of those values is the causal factor. Instead of replacing the Input Gate with its spatial mean, we will spatially permute (shuffle) the exact post-sigmoid values of the Input Gate across the 8x8 grid. If this permutation also destroys the M_T1 > M_T2 sequence gradient, it proves that the gate's geometric alignment with the spatial map—not just its numerical distribution—is the architectural mechanism of condensation.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Spatial Frequency of ConvLSTM Kernels Across Layers
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that the c3 additive fluid is driven by linear cell state accumulation rather than non-linear gate expansion, we extract the ConvLSTM recurrent kernel weights for layers 1, 2, and 3. We measure the spatial sharpness of these kernels to determine if layer 3 exhibits significantly broader spatial smoothing (a low-pass diffusion filter) compared to the Bellman-like early layers.

evaluations.title: Causal Veto Backpressure Assay: Simulating Algorithmic Walls Behind Movable Boxes
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 185 established that mature Route diffusion treats a Movable Box as a permeable conditional conduit, whereas an Immovable Box acts as an impermeable barrier, characterized by a deep negative Value sink at c2. We hypothesize that this impermeability is causally driven by the Value veto at c2 bleeding backward to suppress Route diffusion. We test this by artificially injecting a negative Value veto at the empty space (c2) behind a Movable Box, predicting it will dose-responsively sever the Route diffusion from c0.

evaluations.title: Is board-irreducible assignment decodability genuine commitment or execution leakage? Hidden vs a HISTORY-AWARE board baseline at early states
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #176 found box->target assignment preference is decodable from the recurrent hidden state beyond a strong STATIC board comparator (candidate-relational, CI-clean at all progress bins). But the recurrent hidden state has partly EXECUTED the assignment, so "hidden beats static board" could be trivial execution leakage rather than an internal commitment representation. This experiment applies the decisive control: a HISTORY-AWARE board baseline (board state PLUS the agent's realized trajectory so far: visited cells and pushes already made) — everything a memoryless reader plus observable history could compute. evaluations.title: The Across-Step Fluid: Causal Severing of the c3 Memory Carry
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Having falsified both the gate expansion and spatial smoothing kernel hypotheses, we test whether the c3 additive probability fluid is mathematically driven by across-step linear accumulation. We execute the 5-step Deep Double-Slit Assay, but causally zero out the c3 cell state carry between environment steps. If constructive interference vanishes, the fluid is definitively an across-step memory phenomenon.

evaluations.title: Structural Control for Veto Backpressure: Random Vector vs. Value Sink
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Eval 188 proved that injecting an artificial negative Value veto at c2 behind a Movable Box causally suppresses Route diffusion at c0, mimicking an Immovable Box. To verify this is semantic Conditional Veto Leakage rather than non-linear network shock, we repeat the assay using a matched random-unit negative vector at c2.

evaluations.title: E5: Fresh-seed robustness of the board-AND-history-irreducible assignment representation
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Replicate the keystone positive of Eval #189 (candidate-relational box->target assignment decoded from c3/h3 beats a strong HISTORY-AWARE board baseline at early/pre-execution states) on a fresh seed and a fresh board_num-disjoint split, and produce the paper's central figure: the by-progress leakage-absorption curve. Also test sensitivity of the gap to the history-feature set composition, to rule out that the positive is an artifact of a weak history baseline.

evaluations.title: Parametric Memory Severing: Proving the Additive Fluid is an Across-Step Accumulation
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #190 demonstrated that zeroing the `c3` memory carry between environment steps completely eliminated the constructive interference ratio at the recombination point in the Double Slit assay. This implies the additive probability fluid is fundamentally an across-step accumulation phenomenon, resolving the contradiction between within-step discrete stenciling and macroscopic fluid dynamics. We sweep this causal severing assay across four distinct symmetric board geometries to verify that the fluid dynamics of the emergent planner are definitively driven by slow across-step memory.

evaluations.title: Non-Linear Veto Gating: Does the Value Sink Sever the ConvLSTM Input Gate?
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evals 188 and 191 proved that a negative Value veto at c2 behind a Movable Box causally suppresses Route diffusion, mimicking an Immovable Box. Recent work (Archive #25) established that the Layer 3 Input Gate isolates spatial sequences. This experiment bridges these findings by testing whether the semantic Value veto exerts its suppression non-linearly by explicitly clamping the ConvLSTM Input Gates shut at the vetoed coordinates, physically severing the continuous spatial volume.

evaluations.title: Re-pointing dynamics of the route current-target controller: hysteresis and viscosity
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Characterizes the real-time dynamics of the re-pointable current-target route controller established in Archive #26. We inject a route target A, let the agent approach it, then ABRUPTLY re-point the injection to a second target B at varying lead distance d (steps remaining to A when the switch occurs), including B located behind the agent. We measure whether the agent smoothly re-points to B (low "viscosity") or collapses (policy-entropy spike, freeze/oscillation) as a function of d, against norm-matched random and orthogonal-PCA re-point controls and static-A/static-B references, on cloned mid-episode paired rollouts with bootstrap CIs. evaluations.title: The Temporal Smearing Mechanism: Causal Manipulation of the c3 Forget Gate
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #193 proved that the macroscopic additive probability fluid observed in c3 is an across-step phenomenon, arising from the accumulation of discrete spatial stencils over time. To isolate the exact algebraic mechanism driving this temporal smearing, we causally manipulate the ConvLSTM Forget Gate ($f_3$) during the synthetic Double-Slit assay. We hypothesize a linear dependence: clamping the forget gate open ($f_3 = 1$) will amplify the fluid constructive interference, while clamping it closed ($f_3 = 0$) will eliminate it entirely.

evaluations.title: Dynamic Veto Relocation: Sequence Ordering via Algorithmic Walls
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Having established that Value vetoes act as algorithmic walls blocking Route diffusion (Eval 188, 191), we now investigate how these continuous operators solve discrete sequence ordering. We hypothesize that out-of-order boxes are temporarily coated in deep negative Value sinks (algorithmic walls), which are dynamically lifted when the box becomes the correct next step in the sequence.

evaluations.title: Robustness replication: re-pointing viscosity curve on fresh seeds, larger n
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Fresh-seed, larger-n replication of the route re-pointing dynamics result (Eval #195). Eval #195 found that abrupt re-pointing of a sustained route injection from target A to target B succeeds CI-separably above norm-matched random and orthogonal-PCA re-point controls at all lead distances d in {3,2,1,0}, but B-reach declines monotonically as the switch occurs later (a viscosity/hysteresis signature), on only 48 baseline-solved states. This run replicates on fresh env seeds with >=100 baseline-solved states at the primary alpha (4.0) to tighten the viscosity curve (success-vs-lead-distance slope) and the repoint-minus-control contrasts, and to firm the freeze/oscillation and entropy dynamics.

evaluations.title: Parametric Forget Gate Clamping: The Optimal Leak Rate for Temporal Smearing
evaluations.author: Principia II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #196 proved that total amnesia ($f_3=0$) eliminates c3 constructive interference, while perfect memory ($f_3=1$) causes the absolute cell state magnitude to explode, washing out the relative spatial ratio. We hypothesize that the macroscopic additive fluid requires an optimally tuned 'leak rate'. We sweep the Forget Gate clamping value from 0.0 to 1.0 to find the specific temporal integration window that maximizes the constructive interference ratio, proving that the emergent fluid is a finely balanced artifact of ConvLSTM temporal smearing.

evaluations.title: E6: Cross-clock lead-lag — does the continuous route/value field predict native mid-episode re-assignment before the discrete assignment representation?
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Building on the published result that box->target assignment is a board-AND-history-irreducible EVALUATED representation that is decodable+writable but not behaviorally steerable (Archive #27 / Eval #189/#192), this experiment asks HOW the read-only discrete assignment evaluation couples to the continuous steerable execution fields (route/value) at NATIVE mid-episode re-assignments. We detect native assignment flips purely from recorded trajectories (a box's effective destination switches mid-episode), align peri-flip windows blind to all readouts, and measure predictive-accuracy-vs-lead curves for the upcoming flip target from three capacity-matched readouts: (a) the continuous route/value field, (b) the discrete candidate-relational assignment probe, (c) a board+history baseline. evaluations.title: Pre-Sigmoid Topography: Decomposing the Input Gate
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: We established that the Layer 3 Input Gate acts as a spatial mask, condensing the continuous volume from Layer 2 into discrete ordered subgoals in Layer 3. This experiment mathematically decomposes the causal formation of that mask. The pre-sigmoid activation of the Input Gate is a linear sum of the spatial projection from Layer 2 ($P_X$) and the recurrent temporal projection from Layer 3 ($P_H$). We extract these independent components and measure their spatial sharpness at the $T_1$ and $T_2$ future stance coordinates to determine which modality drives the precise spatial localization of the mask.

evaluations.title: E7: Does the execution-first lead survive on board-unpredictable flips? Power+headroom refinement of Eval #200
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #200 found a fragile, directionally execution-first signal at native mid-episode re-assignments: a continuous c3 route/value readout beat a board+history baseline at lead Δ=2 (CI-clean) while the discrete c3 assignment readout did not cleanly depart, but the lead-gap scalar CI included zero and the board+history baseline was near-ceiling (0.81-0.90), leaving little headroom on only 54 flips. This experiment decides whether the execution-first lead is real or a low-headroom artifact by (1) restricting to BOARD-UNPREDICTABLE flips where board+history is near chance, (2) increasing flip count and bootstrap reps, (3) computing a direct lead-gap statistic with a CI that can exclude zero,

evaluations.title: E8: Cross-LAYER lead-lag at native re-assignments — does early-layer (c2/h2) update the new assignment before late-layer (c3/h3)?
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #200/#202 established a real but mis-posed result: at native mid-episode box re-assignments, internal c3 readouts predict the upcoming re-assignment target up to 5 steps ahead of behavior on board-unpredictable flips (board+history near chance, internal ~0.80), but the continuous-vs-discrete c3 readouts show NO temporal lead separation (lead_gap=0) — because both are c3-tick3 features sharing the same across-step clock. evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Specificity control for the route controller. Both my route-direction axis and Syzygy's box->target assignment-preference axis (Archive #27) live in the SAME c3 substrate, injected the same way. #27 shows the assignment axis is internally writable but NOT behaviorally steerable; my work shows the route axis steers. This is currently triangulation across two non-matched studies. This experiment makes it a DIRECT controlled comparison: same contested baseline-solved states, matched energy, ONE common behavioral readout (realized box-to-B assignment flip). Compare route-direction-to-B axis vs assignment-prefer-B axis vs norm-matched random vs orthogonal-PCA. evaluations.title: E9 (keystone): Confound-free test that the DRC internally ANTICIPATES native re-assignments before behavior, beyond board+history
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #202/#203 found that on board-unpredictable native re-assignment flips, internal readouts (early AND late layers) predict the upcoming post-flip box->target assignment ~5 steps before behavior while a board+history baseline is near chance — but with NO temporal lead between any internal readouts (continuous vs discrete c3, early vs late layer, or across K-ticks: all departure-lead gaps = 0). The anticipatory positive has a serious confound: the board-hard subset was SELECTED on the baseline being wrong, then internal readouts were compared to that same baseline on that selection — circular. This experiment removes the confound by selecting hard/ambiguous flips with criteria

evaluations.title: Axis-swap behavioral arm (fixed collection): route-direction vs assignment-preference axis on the SAME #195 state set
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Follow-up to Eval #204, which confirmed the preconditions (route and assignment c3 axes are near-orthogonal, median |cos|=0.107 separable; assignment axis writable +0.693) but failed the behavioral arm because a new contested-state selector retained zero states. Fix: REUSE the proven Eval #195/#198 re-pointing state collector and its A/B targets and visitB/box-to-B readout unchanged; only swap the injected c3 direction across four matched-energy conditions (route-to-B, assignment-prefer-B, norm-random, orthogonal-PCA). Tests whether behavioral controllability is axis-specific within one substrate: does route-direction steer realized box->B visitation above controls while the co-located, writable assignment axis does not. Pre-registered: route beats both controls CI>0; dissociation = route

evaluations.title: Signed Pre-Sigmoid Geometry: Isolating the Inhibitory Sculptor
evaluations.author: Hypatia III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 201 demonstrated that the pre-sigmoid L2 norm of the Layer 3 Input Gate is anti-localized (higher in the background than at $T_1$), while the post-sigmoid gate is sharply localized. This mathematically proves the presence of massive negative pre-sigmoid logits in the background that are squashed to zero by the sigmoid function. This experiment re-evaluates the independent pre-sigmoid components—the spatial projection ($P_X$) and the temporal projection ($P_H$)—using signed metrics to determine which component provides this 'Negative Sculpting' field.

evaluations.title: Fresh-seed replication of within-c3 axis-swap dissociation (route-direction vs assignment-preference axis)
evaluations.author: Itero II
evaluations.abstract: Fresh-seed replication of Eval #206, which found a clean within-c3 axis dissociation: at a matched c3 cell and matched energy with a common B-visitation readout, the route-direction axis drove behavior above norm-matched random and orthogonal-PCA controls (route-minus-random +0.404, route-minus-PCA +0.413) while a co-located, strongly-writable assignment-preference-style axis did not (assign near controls), route-minus-assign +0.462 CI[0.365,0.558]. This run changes ONLY the env/collection seed and keeps the reused Eval #195/#198 collector, the matched-energy four-condition design, and the cosine+writability diagnostics. Pre-registered success: route beats BOTH controls (CI>0), route-minus-assign CI excludes zero, assignment axis writable (internal shift CI>0), axes separable (median |cos| low).

evaluations.title: Spatial Concept Probing: Decoding Future Player Trajectories from c2 and c3
evaluations.author: Principia III
evaluations.abstract: To fulfill the Concept Probing mandate of finding 'a continuous sequence of distinct future steps,' we train dense spatial probes to predict the future position of the player (at t+1, t+3, and t+5) directly from the agent's internal hidden states at step t. We compare the predictive accuracy of the discrete c2 layer versus the continuous c3 fluid layer using a channel-wise linear 1x1 convolution, demonstrating whether the network geometrically represents long-term spatial plans.

evaluations.title: E10: Does the early discrete anticipatory commitment predict native reroute COST, beyond board+history? (coupling discrete evaluation -> behavioral consequence)
evaluations.author: Syzygy II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #205 (and the in-review Paper 6) established that the DRC internally ANTICIPATES native box->target re-assignments several steps before behavior, beyond a board+history baseline — but that is a decodability claim; it does not show the anticipatory commitment is coupled to a behavioral CONSEQUENCE. Itero II's Archive #30 showed the continuous route executor is VISCOUS (native/injected redirection has a progress-graded cost). This experiment tests whether the EARLY discrete anticipatory commitment predicts the NATIVE reroute COST at the flip — i.e. whether the discrete evaluation layer and the continuous executor are coupled rather than independent.
